messages.text: I drive for DoorDash full time and have a 4 year old. Do we qualify for SNAP or WIC?

Happy to check. I need a few details first.

1. Is it just you and your 4-year-old in the home, or does anyone else live and share food with you?
2. About how much do you make from DoorDash each month before taxes (before expenses are taken out)?
Just me and my daughter, nobody else. Around $2,200 a month before gas and car stuff.

Thanks. Here's where things stand so far, and I have a couple more questions.

**WIC: likely.** Your daughter is under 5, and $2,200 a month is under WIC's limit of $3,337 for a household of 2. The clinic will also do a short health and nutrition check. (Source: [USDA's WIC income limits for July 2026 to June 2027](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926).)

**TennCare/CoverKids: likely for your daughter.** The limit for a child her age in a household of 2 is $2,561 a month. It looks unlikely for you, because the limit for parents is $1,804. You can still apply. (Source: [TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html).)

**SNAP (food assistance): a caseworker needs to look at this.** For DoorDash and other self-employment, SNAP counts your income after business costs like gas and car expenses. My screener can't work that part out. If it counted the full $2,200, it would show you as likely eligible for about $99 a month. That's only a rough estimate. Your real amount could be different, and possibly higher once your business costs are subtracted. A caseworker will make that call.

To tighten the SNAP picture, I need to know:
1. How much is your rent or mortgage each month? Do you pay for heating or cooling, other utilities, or only a phone?
2. Do you pay for child care so you can work? If so, about how much a month?

Also, do you already get SNAP, WIC, or TennCare?

**Where to apply**
- SNAP: [OneDHS online](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or 866-311-4287
- WIC: your local health department clinic, or 1-800-342-5942. More at [tn.gov/health/wic](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html).
- TennCare/CoverKids: [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or 855-259-0701
- Free local help: dial 211

This is only a screening. The state agency makes the final decision, and you can apply even if a screening says it's unlikely.
rent is $900. heating/cooling is separate, I'm not sure of the exact amount. Just a phone bill besides that. no child care. we don't get anything right now, no SNAP, WIC, or TennCare.

With your rent and utilities included, your SNAP estimate went up. WIC and TennCare didn't change.

**SNAP (food assistance): a caseworker needs to look at this.** The screener can't subtract your DoorDash business costs, like gas and car expenses. Without that step, it shows you as likely eligible for about **$277 a month**. That's only an estimate. Your real amount could be higher, because business costs would lower your counted income. Here's how it got there:
- Income before taxes: $2,200
- Minus 20% of earnings ($440) and a standard deduction ($217)
- Minus a housing and utilities deduction ($594.50)
- Countable income: about $948.50, well under the $1,804 limit for 2 people

Tennessee's SNAP income limit is also unsettled. USDA's official limit is 130% of poverty, but 200% has been reported. At $2,200 you're under the official limit of $2,345 either way. Because you pay heating or cooling, I used Tennessee's standard utility allowance. That figure is the latest published one and may be out of date. (Sources: [USDA's FY 2027 SNAP limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola), [USDA's utility allowance table](https://www.fns.usda.gov/sites/default/files/resource-files/2026-05-21-SUA-Table-FY26.xlsx).)

**WIC: likely** for your daughter. Expect a short health and nutrition check at the clinic. ([USDA WIC limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926))

**TennCare/CoverKids: likely for your daughter, unlikely for you.** You can still apply for yourself. ([TennCare guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html))

**Good to know**
- SNAP has a savings limit of $3,000 in cash and bank accounts under federal rules. I didn't ask about your savings, so check that before you apply.
- I used a placeholder age for you, since age didn't seem to change the result. If you're 60 or older, tell me, because that could matter for SNAP.
- Keep records of your DoorDash earnings and car costs. The caseworker will probably ask for them.

**Where to apply**
- SNAP: [OneDHS online](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or 866-311-4287
- WIC: your local health department clinic, or 1-800-342-5942 ([tn.gov/health/wic](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html))
- TennCare/CoverKids: [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or 855-259-0701
- Free local help: dial 211

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides, and you can apply even if a screening says it's unlikely. Please report your income and costs accurately, because overpayments have to be paid back.
